From 8821e857759be9db3cde337ad328b71fe5c8a55f Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Larysa Zaremba <larysa.zaremba@intel.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 12:12:50 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] xdp: produce a warning when calculated tailroom is negative
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

Many ethernet drivers report xdp Rx queue frag size as being the same as
DMA write size. However, the only user of this field, namely
bpf_xdp_frags_increase_tail(), clearly expects a truesize.

Such difference leads to unspecific memory corruption issues under certain
circumstances, e.g. in ixgbevf maximum DMA write size is 3 KB, so when
running xskxceiver's XDP_ADJUST_TAIL_GROW_MULTI_BUFF, 6K packet fully uses
all DMA-writable space in 2 buffers. This would be fine, if only
rxq->frag_size was properly set to 4K, but value of 3K results in a
negative tailroom, because there is a non-zero page offset.

We are supposed to return -EINVAL and be done with it in such case, but due
to tailroom being stored as an unsigned int, it is reported to be somewhere
near UINT_MAX, resulting in a tail being grown, even if the requested
offset is too much (it is around 2K in the abovementioned test). This later
leads to all kinds of unspecific calltraces.

diff --git a/net/core/filter.c b/net/core/filter.c
index d6fafb3633b0..a77d23fe2359 100644
--- a/net/core/filter.c
+++ b/net/core/filter.c
@@ -4150,13 +4150,14 @@ static int bpf_xdp_frags_increase_tail(struct xdp_buff *xdp, int offset)
 	struct skb_shared_info *sinfo = xdp_get_shared_info_from_buff(xdp);
 	skb_frag_t *frag = &sinfo->frags[sinfo->nr_frags - 1];
 	struct xdp_rxq_info *rxq = xdp->rxq;
-	unsigned int tailroom;
+	int tailroom;
 
 	if (!rxq->frag_size || rxq->frag_size > xdp->frame_sz)
 		return -EOPNOTSUPP;
 
 	tailroom = rxq->frag_size - skb_frag_size(frag) -
 		   skb_frag_off(frag) % rxq->frag_size;
+	WARN_ON_ONCE(tailroom < 0);
 	if (unlikely(offset > tailroom))
 		return -EINVAL;

2.34.1

The patch fixes a bug in the XDP tailroom calculation where a negative tailroom value was incorrectly treated as a large positive number due to an unsigned integer type. This caused memory corruption when drivers incorrectly reported `frag_size` as DMA write size instead of truesize.

**Changes in `net/core/filter.c`:**

1. **`tailroom` variable type changed from `unsigned int` to `int`** – This ensures that the result of the calculation (`rxq->frag_size - skb_frag_size(frag) - skb_frag_off(frag) % rxq->frag_size`) can hold negative values, which previously wrapped to near `UINT_MAX`.

2. **Added `WARN_ON_ONCE(tailroom < 0)`** – When the tailroom is negative, this warning alerts administrators to driver misconfiguration (e.g., inconsistent `frag_size`), providing a diagnostic hint before the subsequent check `offset > tailroom` is performed.

The type change is prerequisite for the warning to work meaningfully; together they prevent the erroneous tail growth that led to the reported memory corruption and crashes.

Fixes: bf25146a5595 ("bpf: add frags support to the bpf_xdp_adjust_tail() API")
Reviewed-by: Aleksandr Loktionov <aleksandr.loktionov@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Toke Høiland-Jørgensen <toke@redhat.com>
Acked-by: Martin KaFai Lau <martin.lau@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Larysa Zaremba <larysa.zaremba@intel.com>

Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

Here is the root cause:
The tailroom calculation in `bpf_xdp_frags_increase_tail()` can become negative when drivers report `frag_size` as DMA write size (e.g., 3 KB in ixgbevf) instead of the expected truesize (e.g., 4 KB), especially with non-zero page offsets. The variable `tailroom` was declared as `unsigned int`, causing negative values to wrap to a very large positive number, which bypassed the `offset > tailroom` check and allowed excessive tail growth. This led to memory corruption and crashes. The fix changes `tailroom` to a signed `int` and adds a `WARN_ON_ONCE` to detect negative values.

Here is the patch:
 
 static int bpf_xdp_frags_increase_tail(struct xdp_buff *xdp, int offset)
 {
 	struct skb_shared_info *sinfo = xdp_get_shared_info_from_buff(xdp);
 	skb_frag_t *frag = &sinfo->frags[sinfo->nr_frags - 1];
 	struct xdp_rxq_info *rxq = xdp->rxq;
-	unsigned int tailroom;
+	int tailroom;
 
 	if (!rxq->frag_size || rxq->frag_size > xdp->frame_sz)
 		return -EOPNOTSUPP;
 
 	tailroom = rxq->frag_size - skb_frag_size(frag) -
 		   skb_frag_off(frag) % rxq->frag_size;
+	WARN_ON_ONCE(tailroom < 0);
 	if (unlikely(offset > tailroom))
 		return -EINVAL;
 
 	memset(skb_frag_address(frag) + skb_frag_size(frag), 0, offset);
 	skb_frag_size_add(frag, offset);
 	sinfo->xdp_frags_size += offset;
 	if (rxq->mem.type == MEM_TYPE_XSK_BUFF_POOL)
 		xsk_buff_get_tail(xdp)->data_end += offset;
 
 	return 0;
 }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
unsigned int tailroom;
```
Reason: When `tailroom` is computed as a negative value (e.g., `rxq->frag_size - skb_frag_size(frag) - skb_frag_off(frag) % rxq->frag_size`), storing it in an `unsigned int` causes it to wrap to a large positive number. This makes the subsequent check `if (unlikely(offset > tailroom))` always false, so the function does not return -EINVAL and an oversized tail growth occurs, leading to memory corruption.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
int tailroom;
```
and
```c
WARN_ON_ONCE(tailroom < 0);
```
Reason: Changing `tailroom` to `signed int` ensures that a negative value is properly detected. Adding `WARN_ON_ONCE(tailroom < 0)` alerts when a driver provides an incorrect `frag_size` (a spuriously negative tailroom), helping prevent future misuse while the function still returns `-EINVAL` if `offset > tailroom` (which now correctly rejects negative tailroom).
